destination.name: Penrith
destination.tagline: Western Sydney's river city, with an Olympic whitewater course and a zoo within a short drive.
destination.description: Penrith is a suburb 55 km west of the Sydney CBD on the Nepean River and the administrative centre of its council area. North of the Sydney 2000 rowing lake in Penrith Lakes, a system of flooded quarries, lies Penrith Whitewater Stadium, the only pump-powered artificial whitewater slalom course in the Southern Hemisphere. Visitors can book rafting and kayaking there, and Sydney Zoo at Bungarribee adds African, Asian and Australian animals. The Blue Mountains Line makes it the first major stop before the mountains.
whyVisit: See African animals at Sydney Zoo

goodToKnow.title: Whitewater is booked
goodToKnow.detail: Penrith Whitewater Stadium has no fixed public hours; rafting and kayaking are sold as booked sessions at about $135 for an adult.

goodToKnow.title: Two separate sites
goodToKnow.detail: Sydney Zoo is at Bungarribee in Western Sydney Parklands, apart from the whitewater course at Penrith Lakes; it opens 9 AM to 5 PM and an adult ticket is $45 to $55.

goodToKnow.title: Hotter than the city
goodToKnow.detail: Penrith runs a few degrees hotter than central Sydney in spring and summer, so book water sessions and zoo days for mornings.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} avoid Penrith's long hot summers, which run a few degrees warmer than central Sydney, and suit paddling and a day at the zoo.
